A popular action role-playing game. Every day. All day.

Like most action role-playing games, you tend to want to cull most of the loot that drops from what you pick up. It’s a learning process though and goes a long way in making your experience most efficient and pleasant.
Get an item filter. A popular game’s filter is a good place to start. Different levels will be more strict about what they show. It’s a good way to learn.

The sound and coloring will help some, but honestly, that kind of knowledge is a big part of the game and what allows the veterans to go so fast.

Time will teach you. When in doubt, take an item you think might be good and put it up for 1-2c. If after a minute or two you get five whispers at once about buying the item, pull it and look it up. Figure out what made it worth more.

If you really want to learn and learn quickly, keep a popular item price tracking website open and look up items as they appear. You’ll see a rough estimate of there current prices and the direction their price is trending. Or look up the item on a community trade site and see what others are selling it for. Remember to ignore the first five or ten entries as “price fixers” will list a couple of items for very low prices in order to trick newer players into selling it for too little. This process can and will get tedious, but again, you’re learning.

Finally, there’s also a trade macro which is a script for a popular automation tool. It’s allowed per the game developer’s terms of service and most serious traders use it. I’m not a fan because I don’t think it integrates well with the game (too immersion breaking for me; I know that’s ironic compared to alt-tabbing). But, it can help you see what the average price of an item is in game and why (because of T1 affixes, enchants, corrupted implicits, rarity).

Most importantly, don’t forget to do whatever is fun for you. It’s a game, and there’ll always be ways to min/max the way you play. And yes, for some, being most efficient is a kind of fun in and of itself, don’t let it jeopardize your enjoyment of the core game loop. Explore, kill shit, get loot. Rinse, repeat.

Welcome to the game. You’re one of us now. 

Every single player has gone through something like this. Everyone. It’s a rite of passage.

As for fixing your character. First, you should know that long term, any characters you have sitting in standard will get free respecs eventually (usually after major changes and new league starts).

For the short term, you know the two option: reroll or buy orbs of regret. Here’s how I would choose. First, how many points total do you need to respec? 40? 60? The entire tree plus your ascendancy? Get yourself a final cost. Second, deduct 20 assuming you still have the free respec points. If you don’t know what I mean, some of the side quests in the main story reward free respec points. Third, check how long it took to get you where you are by typing “/played” in chat. 30 hours? Any new character you start will be faster, but still, that can be quite lengthy.

If you’re already 75 and made it to maps, you should already have about a dozen orbs of regret. Personally, I think it would be more time efficient to buy the orbs of regret (farming any currency you need to buy them via the chaos recipe) and just respec that way. I would also stick to your ascendancy (hopefully you didn’t completely botch that), as there’s usually something viable for most ascendancy paths. 

If you’re curious about your ascendancy and typical points taken, check the website and see how others specced with your ascendancy and similar skills and items.
